I'm leaning toward keeping the span minimal, annotating "breast and ovarian cancer" as the composite mention and excluding "familial" since it's more about inheritance pattern than a distinct disease form. Applying similar logic to "sporadic breast and ovarian cancers" and "breast carcinoma" mentions, treating "breast and ovarian cancers" as a composite and moving on to evaluate "breast carcinoma" separately.

For later instances like "breast cancer roughly equal to BRCA1," I'm weighing whether this counts as SpecificDisease versus a broader disease class mention.

Same type found in familial forms, I note, with BRCA1 as an exception—it contributes heavily to familial breast and ovarian cancer but has very low somatic mutation rates in sporadic cases, and I'm continuing to track the precise character offsets for each word.

This suggests other genes are likely the main targets for somatic mutation in breast carcinoma. I'm now moving into tracking a second, recently identified familial breast cancer gene, continuing the character-counting pattern.

I'm counting character positions through the passage, noting that carriers of one mutant allele face elevated breast cancer risk, and their tumors lose the wild-type allele via heterozygous deletion. I'm also tracking that the BRCA2 coding sequence is quite large.

The BRCA2 coding sequence spans 26 exons across 10,443 bp, and I'm noting the plan here is to examine BRCA2 mutation rates in sporadic breast cancers and a panel of cell lines.

Interestingly, mutations in BRCA2 turn out to be rare across cancers including breast carcinoma itself, though one cell line derived from a pancreatic tumor shows a likely germline mutation.

I'm now finishing the offset tracking for this sentence and sanity-checking word lengths like "heterozygous," "susceptibility," and "involvement" against my counts to make sure they line up before I start tagging the actual disease mention spans, starting with "breast carcinoma" and "cancers."
